The component text confirms this is more than three button verbs: object nouns also drift (`user`, `member`, `team`, `seat`), and `TeamList` even links a seat action from a team surface. I’m checking the detector definitions now so I can distinguish the two findings precisely rather than treating the duplicate-looking reports as separate defects.

The supplied `crimes scan --format json` confirms one underlying drift reported through two detector lenses: `delete`, `remove`, and `archive` each appear in at least two of the three components.

I’d canonicalize on **Delete + target noun**:

| Component | Current labels | Canonical label |
|---|---|---|
| `UserList` | “Delete user”, “Remove member” | **Delete user** |
| `TeamList` | “Archive team” | **Delete team** |
| `TeamList` seat action | “Delete the seat” | **Delete seat** |
| `SeatList` | “Remove member”, “Archive member” | **Delete seat** |

“Delete” is preferable because the scenario defines the operation as destructive. “Archive” usually implies recoverability, while “Remove” can mean merely detaching membership; using either would blur the actual consequence.

I’d refactor [SeatList.tsx](/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/evals/fixtures/05-stress-ia-drift/src/components/SeatList.tsx) first. It:

- Anchors both reported findings.
- Contains both noncanonical verbs and no canonical `delete`.
- Calls seats “members,” adding target ambiguity.
- Has two differently labelled links to the same `/seats/manage` destination.

Then I’d update [UserList.tsx](/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/evals/fixtures/05-stress-ia-drift/src/components/UserList.tsx) and [TeamList.tsx](/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/evals/fixtures/05-stress-ia-drift/src/components/TeamList.tsx).

Detector mapping:

- `action_label_drift`: the broader cross-surface rule. It examines JSX labels plus other IA/nav label signals. Replacing `Remove` and `Archive` with `Delete` establishes one action vocabulary.
- `copy_ia_drift`: the frontend-copy-specific rule. It considers only JSX label literals. Aligning the full visible strings—verb, noun, and article style—addresses this finding.

On this fixture their evidence is identical because every qualifying signal comes from JSX `label` props. They are two views of the same inconsistency, not two independent bugs.

One caveat: changing `SeatList` alone may make both findings disappear because the conservative heuristic requires three aliases, each present in at least two files. The remaining `Remove` in `UserList` and `Archive` in `TeamList` would still be inconsistent, so all three components should be aligned even if the intermediate scan is clean.
